inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $170M (us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation) plus $72M cash withholding taxes on net-share settlement (us-gaap:PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation, financing activities). Hilton publishes no combined figure in its Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (that line is the $170M expense only), so the two are summed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases $3,182M; 9M-2026 $2,633M cash (8.2M shares for $2,602M ex excise tax), ~$2.2B left on the $18.0B programme at 30 September 2026. The flat share count is fully funded: Hilton retires ~10M shares a year, far more than SBC issues. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (SBC is expensed; count held flat). They are partly DEBT-funded: 9M-2026 buybacks + dividends of ~$2.7B against ~$1.7B of free cash flow, with total debt up ~$1.0B since year-end. That borrowing is charged once, as higher net debt in the bridge; the model gives no credit for the per-share accretion.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted ~225.1M at 30 September 2026: 223,093,590 shares outstanding on the Q3-2026 10-Q balance sheet plus ~2.0M dilutive RSU/PSU/options (Q3-2026 weighted diluted 226M vs weighted basic 224M). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Q3-2026 10-Q, 30 September 2026: long-term debt incl. finance leases $12,731M + current maturities $626M = $13,357M (no double count of the current portion), less cash $774M (restricted cash $56M excluded). Finance lease liabilities sit in debt because their cost (ROU amortisation in D&A, interest) is outside EBITDA. Operating lease liabilities ($851M at FY2025) are EXCLUDED because operating lease cost is inside EBITDA under US GAAP.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: FY2025 OCF $2,129M less capex for property & equipment $101M less capitalized software $84M = $1,944M (Hilton's own free-cash-flow definition). The Metrics CSV FreeCashFlow of $2,028M deducts PP&E only. Contract acquisition costs (key money) are classified INSIDE operating activities by Hilton, so they are already in OCF and need no further deduction.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0-1.1 for a fee-based lodging franchisor -> cost of equity ~9.2-9.7%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (FY2025 interest expense $620M on ~$11.7B average debt), ~4.0% after tax. Market weights: equity ~$84B vs debt $13.4B -> D/V ~14%. WACC = 0.86 x 9.4% + 0.14 x 4.0% = ~8.6%, rounded to 8.5%. UNCHANGED on this update. Leverage judgment for a debt-funded-buyback name: negative book equity (-$6.6B) is irrelevant to the weights, which are market-value; net debt is ~3.1x guided FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA (~3.9x TTM GAAP EBITDA) and has drifted up ~$0.25B in the quarter, which is not enough to re-lever beta or move the rate. No leverage premium is stacked on the WACC: the leverage risk is charged once, through the full $12.6B net-debt deduction, the recession bear path with a 15x cap, and the 25% bear weight. The rate is held IDENTICAL across scenarios for the same reason. What would move it: net debt/Adjusted EBITDA sustained above ~3.5x (management's 3.0-3.5x target breached), a rating downgrade to high-yield territory lifting the marginal cost of debt, or a 10y UST move of more than ~75bp.
inputs.lease_treatment: One treatment: operating leases (owned/leased hotel segment) are an operating cost inside EBITDA and their liabilities are NOT added to net debt; finance leases are in net debt and their ROU amortisation/interest are outside EBITDA. Never both.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests $30M (30 September 2026) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated. Immaterial (<0.1% of EV).
inputs.tax_basis: Cash tax rate 25% on EBIT, unlevered: between the 21% federal statutory rate and the 29.5% FY2025 GAAP effective rate (state, foreign, unrecognised-tax-benefit accruals); FY2025 cash taxes paid $523M on pretax income $2,072M = 25.2%. The interest tax shield is carried in the after-tax cost of debt in WACC, not in the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: operating company, US, asset-light franchisor). Negative book equity (-$6.6B at Q3-2026) is the product of a decade of debt-funded buybacks against a fee stream that does not need the capital; it is not a routing trigger (no distress, no going-concern issue, interest cover ~4.5x on GAAP EBITDA) and the equity-CAGR growth anchor is simply undefined for this ticker, so revenue and owner-FCF CAGRs are used instead. EBITDA in the CSV is GAAP operating income + D&A on GROSS revenue (including ~$3.5B+ of zero-margin cost reimbursements from managed and franchised properties); it is ~$0.8B below Hilton's 'Adjusted EBITDA' because it carries the reimbursed-cost net loss, SBC and other add-backs. The margin paths below are on that GAAP basis and must not be compared with Hilton's adjusted-EBITDA guidance without that bridge. Owner FCF (last_fcf) is levered (after $648M cash interest) and is an anchor only; the projections are unlevered from components and net debt is deducted at the end. FY0 is FY2025; year 1 is FY2026 discounted a full period even though more than ten months have elapsed (conservative by most of a year of discounting, ~7% of value; kept for comparability with the prior version and to be re-based when the FY2026 10-K lands). Working capital: Hilton runs a structural float from Hilton Honors co-brand card prepayments and deferred revenue (+$194M in FY2025 alone; contract liabilities $2.35B), captured conservatively at 15% of the revenue change in the base case versus ~40% observed in FY2025. Interest income is immaterial against $12.3B of net debt and is not stripped. Price is a regular-session close (see price_as_of), not an after-hours print. UPDATE of the 2026-09-29 build: anchors refreshed to the Q3-2026 10-Q and only the FY2026 guidance-year drivers re-judged; see reconciliation and update_notes.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr tempered by fee algorithm (NUG 6-7% + RevPAR 3-3.5% guided for FY2026; total revenue grows slower than fees because reimbursements and the ownership segment dilute it). Equity CAGR is undefined: book equity is negative.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR cannot be computed (shareholders' equity negative since FY2019 from debt-funded buybacks). 5-year CAGRs start from the FY2020 COVID trough (revenue $4.3B, EPS -$2.58) and are not meaningful; the 3-year figures (FY2022-FY2025) and the FY2019-FY2025 6-year revenue CAGR of 4.1% bracket the real trend.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = OCF - PP&E capex - SBC add-back - equity-award withholding taxes (capitalized software not available in the CSV for FY2022, so excluded from both endpoints for consistency): FY2022 $1,422M -> FY2025 $1,786M = 7.9% 3yr CAGR vs 7.3% on reported FCF. SBC has grown slightly slower than cash flow (FY2022 $162M -> FY2025 $170M), so SBC is not eating the reported growth here.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7.0% (UNCHANGED): 9M-2026 revenue $9,603M is +7.3% YoY (Q3 +6.6%) and Q4 is guided softer (RevPAR +3.0-3.5%, midterms, Middle East), which lands the year at ~6.8-7.0%. Decelerates 0.5pp/yr as NUG normalises toward 5% and RevPAR toward inflation; 3% terminal. Years 2-10 unchanged.
base.margin_rationale: GAAP EBITDA margin FY2025 23.8%; 9M-2026 27.0% (9M-2025 24.8%). FY2026 raised 25.5% -> 26.2%: Adjusted EBITDA guidance $4.06-4.08B less a GAAP bridge now running ~$0.65B (9M-2026 bridge $417M vs $558M a year earlier) on ~$12.87B revenue. FY2027 nudged 26.0% -> 26.3% only so the path does not model a decline nobody is forecasting. FY2028 onward UNCHANGED (26.5% rising to 28.5% by FY2035): the 9M beat is mostly a smaller reimbursed-cost net loss, which is lumpy and reverses, not a step-change in fee margin.
base.capex_rationale: PP&E $101M + capitalized software $84M = 1.5% of FY2025 revenue; FY2024 1.8%. Held at 1.6%. D&A 1.5% (FY2025 $177M).
base.narrative: Fee algorithm intact: mid-single-digit unit growth plus low-single-digit RevPAR, margin drifting up with mix, all FCF returned.
base.sbc_rationale: FY2026 raised 2.0% -> 2.3% of revenue: 9M-2026 SBC expense $165M (+22% YoY) plus $73M withholding taxes implies ~$295M for the year. Glide re-anchored at 2.3% and declining 0.1pp/yr until it rejoins the prior path at year 6 (1.8%); years 6-10 unchanged.

bull.narrative: Record 543k-room pipeline converts at 7%+ NUG for longer, international (India, Middle East, APAC) and conversion brands keep the runway open, RevPAR holds 3-4%, fee mix drives GAAP EBITDA margin past 30%, and the Honors float captures 20% of growth.
bull.growth_rates_note: Year 1 cut 8.5% -> 7.3%: with 9M at +7.3% an 8.5% year is no longer reachable. Years 2-10 unchanged.

bear.narrative: A 2027-28 travel recession (RevPAR -6 to -8%, as in 2009 scale rather than 2020 scale), developer financing tightens so NUG slips toward 4%, owner-favourable fee concessions to hold conversion share compress margin, and the recovery settles at a lower long-run growth and a 15x terminal cap for a cyclical fee stream on a levered balance sheet.
bear.growth_rates_note: Year 1 raised 5.0% -> 6.5%: nine months are booked at +7.3%, so even a weak Q4 (+4%) gives ~6.5%. The recession path (years 2-3) is unchanged.

scenario_narratives.base: Hilton keeps executing its asset-light algorithm: net unit growth of 6-7% (6.0% trailing at Q3-2026; record pipeline of ~3,869 hotels / 543k rooms, nearly half under construction) fading toward 4-5% by the early 2030s as the base grows, system-wide RevPAR of 4.0-4.5% in FY2026 (event-boosted) normalising toward 2-3%, and the ownership/reimbursement drag shrinking as a share of revenue so GAAP EBITDA margin rises from 23.8% (FY2025) through ~26.2% (FY2026) to about 28.5% by FY2035. SBC runs ~2.3% of revenue in FY2026 and glides to 1.6%, capex ~1.6%, and the Honors co-brand float contributes a modest working-capital tailwind. Value is discounted at a uniform 8.5% USD WACC with 3% terminal growth; Gordon binds below the 20x cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The axes that matter are pipeline conversion and RevPAR durability. In the bull case the 543k-room pipeline converts at 7%+ NUG for several more years, conversion brands (Spark, Curio, Tapestry) and international markets (India, Middle East, Japan) keep the signings pace ahead of openings, business transient demand sustains RevPAR of 3-4%, and the growing share of fee income pushes GAAP EBITDA margin past 30%. Hilton Honors' ~270M members widen the direct-booking advantage, and the credit-card float captures 20% of incremental revenue.
scenario_narratives.bear: Lodging is classically cyclical and Hilton now carries $12.6B of net debt (~3.1x Adjusted, ~3.9x GAAP EBITDA) with a -$6.6B book-equity deficit and buybacks running ahead of free cash flow. The bear case is a 2027-28 recession: RevPAR falls 6-8% (a 2009-scale shock, not 2020), fee income drops with it, developer construction financing tightens so NUG slips toward 4%, and Hilton concedes owner-favourable fee adjustments (flagged in Q2-2026 commentary; Middle East RevPAR -12% for 9M-2026 and China softness show how quickly regional fee income moves) to defend conversion share against Marriott, IHG, Wyndham and Choice. Margins compress to ~22.5% at the trough and recover only to 26%. Buybacks pause but debt service is maintained; the terminal cap is cut to 15x for a cyclical fee stream on a levered balance sheet.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25. Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because travel demand is highly cyclical, net debt is ~3.1x Adjusted EBITDA (~3.9x GAAP) with negative book equity and debt-funded buybacks (no balance-sheet cushion if fees fall), and owner fee concessions have been flagged. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires sustained 7%+ NUG, RevPAR durability AND margin expansion beyond 30% together, and the current price already discounts most of that path (trailing GAAP P/E ~50x). Q3-2026 did not shift the balance: RevPAR guidance up, EBITDA guidance midpoint barely moved, revenue slightly light.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Hilton is one of the best fee-based business models in the market: capital-light, high incremental margins, a loyalty network with ~270M members and a record development pipeline. The valuation question is not quality but price. The house DCF expenses SBC, deducts the $12.6B of net debt that funded the buybacks, discounts at a uniform 8.5% and caps the terminal multiple at 20x; on those terms the market price sits well above intrinsic value and implies either a materially lower required return or a longer runway of 7%+ growth than the base case grants. The negative book equity is a capital-allocation artefact, not a distress signal, but it means the entire equity value rests on the durability of the fee stream through a downturn.
key_risks_to_valuation: Travel-demand recession: RevPAR and fee income fall together; with ~3-4x leverage, no equity cushion and buybacks already exceeding free cash flow, repurchases pause and the multiple derates
Pipeline-to-open conversion slows if developer financing tightens (higher-for-longer rates)
Owner-favourable fee concessions to hold conversion share against Marriott/IHG/Wyndham/Choice compress fee margin
Premium multiple (trailing GAAP P/E ~50x, ~45x owner FCF) leaves little room for execution misses
GAAP EBITDA basis includes zero-margin cost reimbursements; a change in the reimbursed-cost net loss (Honors, marketing funds) moves the modelled margin without changing fees
Discount-rate sensitivity: a terminal-heavy, long-duration fee stream loses value quickly as required return rises
Stub-period conservatism: FY2026 is discounted a full year with ten months elapsed, understating value by roughly 7%; this does not close the gap to the market price
